name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (GB202, compute capability 12.0)
notes: Published figures, not a measurement: no device run has confirmed any of them, and none has run here. launch_ns, link_ns, memory_efficiency, occupancy_to_saturate and memory_latency_ns are assumptions, the same on every packaged card, marked as such below.

documents.whitepaper: NVIDIA RTX Blackwell GPU Architecture whitepaper V1.1, Appendix A, Table 3, the GeForce RTX 5090 column (https://images.nvidia.com/aem-dam/Solutions/geforce/blackwell/nvidia-rtx-blackwell-gpu-architecture.pdf)
documents.guide: CUDA Programming Guide 13.4.2, Compute Capabilities, Tables 30 and 31 (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html)

source.sms: RTX Blackwell whitepaper: 170 SMs of 128 CUDA cores, GPU boost clock 2407 MHz.
source.dram_gbps: RTX Blackwell whitepaper: 32 GB GDDR7 at 1792 GB/s.
source.flops: RTX Blackwell whitepaper: Peak FP32 104.8 TFLOPS and Peak INT32 TOPS 104.8, since Blackwell's cores issue either. f64 is derived: FP64 at 1/64 of FP32 (Guide, Table 30).
source.tensor: RTX Blackwell whitepaper, dense (the sparse figures are twice these), with FP32 accumulate: FP16 and BF16 209.5, FP8 419, FP4 1676, TF32 104.8 TFLOPS. The model reads tensor_f16; the others are recorded for a reader.
source.link_gbps: RTX Blackwell whitepaper: PCI Express Gen 5; at x16, 64 GB/s each way, before protocol overhead.
source.occupancy: CUDA Programming Guide 13.4.2, Compute Capabilities, Tables 30 and 31 (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html), 12.x column: 64 K registers, 48 warps (1536 threads) and 100 KB of shared memory an SM; the CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9, section 20, says for each of 8.x, 9.0, 10.x and 12.0 that the 1 KB of shared memory not made available to a thread block is reserved for system use (shared_reserved); the CUDA Occupancy Calculator allocates registers a warp at a time in units of 256 (register_unit). No limit on resident blocks per SM is applied here.
source.shared_bytes_per_clock: CUDA C++ Programming Guide: shared memory has 32 banks, each 32 bits wide a clock cycle.
source.memory_latency_ns: Assumed. NVIDIA publishes no device-memory latency and no run here has measured one; it prices only a pipeline's asynchronous copies, as the bytes in flight over this latency. Every packaged card assumes the same 500 ns.
